content:
We need to find template that when applied to molecule C#CC(=O)OCC (propargyl acetate? Actually it's propargyl acetate: propargyl acetate is C#CC(=O)OCH2CH3). Reaction: Still-Gennari HWE forms Z-alkene from aldehyde + phosphonate ester. But here we have alkyne to alkene? The description: triple bond of an alkyne is changed to a single bond. So maybe the reaction is a reduction? But they mention HWE forming C=C and carboxylic ester formed. The target molecule is C#CC(=O)OCC. The retrosynthetic step: break C-C double bond formed (so product has alkene) and carboxylic ester formed. In reverse, we need precursors: an aldehyde and a phosphonate ester? The product is an alkyne? Wait forward reaction: aldehyde + phosphonate ester -> alkene (Z) + carboxylate? Actually HWE: phosphonate + aldehyde -> alkene + phosphate byproduct. Still-Gennari uses bis(trifluoroethyl) phosphonate to give Z-alkene. So product is alkene, not alkyne. Our target molecule is alkyne with ester. So maybe the reaction described is reverse: we have alkyne ester, we want to go back to aldehyde + phosphonate? But the forward reaction would break C-P bond, break C-C bond (maybe between phosphonate carbon and P?), break C-O bond (the O of the phosphonate?), and form C=C and C-O (ester). Also triple bond changes to single bond (so alkyne to alkene). So the target is alkene ester? Wait they say "triple bond of an alkyne is changed to a single bond". So forward reaction: alkyne -> alkene. So starting material is alkyne, product is alkene. Our given molecule is C#CC(=O)OCC which contains alkyne (C#C) and an ester. So that is the starting material? Actually it has alkyne, so forward reaction would convert that alkyne to alkene, also form carboxylic ester (already present). So maybe the product is something like CH2=CH-COOEt? That would be ethyl acrylate (C=CC(=O)OCC). Indeed ethyl acrylate SMILES: C=CC(=O)OCC. Starting alkyne is propargyl acetate? Wait propargyl acetate is C#CC(=O)OCH3? Actually propargyl acetate is C#CC(=O)OCH3. Our SMILES C#CC(=O)OCC is propargyl acetate with ethyl? That's propargyl acetate ethyl? Actually it's propargyl acetate ethyl? The product ethyl acrylate is C=CC(=O)OCC. So the reaction converts propargyl acetate to ethyl acrylate via Still-Gennari? Not typical. But we just need to find template that matches this transformation.

We need to search template catalog for a template that when applied to target molecule (product) yields precursors? Wait the task: "return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule below (provided as available input data), reproduces the reaction". The input data: from make_5_lvl2-apply_template-4 answer: '[]' meaning applying some template gave no precursors. We need to find correct template.

We have to search templates by criteria: functional groups formed: C-C double bonds, carboxylic esters. Broken: C-C triple bonds. That we attempted and got empty list. Maybe need to include bonds broken/formed. Could also include functional groups broken: alkyne? Not in list. Use "C-C triple bonds" as broken functional group (exists). We used that earlier and got empty list. Maybe need to include also "carboxylic esters" formed. Already did. Still empty.

Maybe need to search by bonds: broken bond between sp carbon and sp carbon (triple). Not sure.

Alternative: Use search without functional groups, just bonds. Could try bonds_broken: "6-6" (triple bond) and bonds_formed: "6-6" (double). But we tried something similar.

Maybe the template ID is known? Could be a known HWE template. Could try to get template list by searching for functional_groups_formed ["C-C double bonds"] only.
